chapter: WPA band and 1930s New Orleans bands
title: Eddie Miller, Fazola and learning to read in the band
summary: Sal describes the Miller family band, clarinet players quitting, and Fazola struggling to read music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: What was Eddie Miller playing then? Tennis.

And did he play any clarinet or things? Fine. Nothing, nothing, nothing as good as Fodger. He played rap. I started clarinet kind of style of rap and he got a full rap. Well, one night, Eddie Miller was playing with a band by the name of Martin. They had four Millers in the band. Now, Benny Miller was playing the guitar, the little red guy. Eddie was playing saxophone clarinet. And Chuck Miller was playing the drums. And the little band was doing a carol. So, I went back there one night, Michael Manon, Louis Street. And I went to play clarinet. He said, man, that guy plays good, man. Well, Harry, she was always, in those days, I'm telling you about Harry, now. He's clarinet player. He would always quit, to independent. He walked in like that until Harry, all dressed up, you know, and the clarinet wrapped up in newspaper. No, no, no, no, I want to leave, you know what I mean? Quit in the band again, so he quit. So, Buddy said, hey man, can you give me clarinet player? I wasn't like that. He said, go get a ring with Boyk, man. I was like, I go see Raymond. He came up there. He said, where's he, John? I remember him, he said, oh, it's too hard, man. Too hard? Yeah. Too hard, man. I don't know where I want to go. I don't want to play that, but it's too hard, man. I said, well, I want to be clarinet player. I see, I believe I got that. Farzola on the same metal saxophone. He couldn't fake it. Everything was read, man. So the man, the man owned the place, built us some stands, you know. He couldn't read and we couldn't. Ta, ta, ta, ta, ta, ta. Couldn't read that, man. Farzola would seem under the saxophone. He couldn't fake it. Everything was read, man. So the man owned the place, built us some stands, you know. He couldn't read and we couldn't. So we started reading Sonny Ball. Ta, ta, ta, ta, ta, ta. Couldn't read that, man. Farzola would seem under the saxophone. Ain't no way there, see. Then we got Eddie Miller from Kerala's band to play clarinet. And he started playing. And he had that nigga next door, the band leader, good musician, man. Old man, Robert Shaw. He had a suitor playing drum next door. He said, he had a band. Nigga was half white, you know. He said, that fat boy playing up there, he's still in the saxophone. That's a fat musician. He said, it's farzola. Yeah. We had to come around with your boys, you know. He could get more experience with you all. But he'd be good in no time. And sure enough, man.
